name: Irene Baptiste
life: “I still remember washing a restaurant apron until it turned pink.” On Wednesday, near Breakwater Way, Irene stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I put three different loads in to test my theory and dyed my best shirt.
appearance: Irene has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow. Look for a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears. Away from the heat of the kitchen, the familiar outfit is a striped cotton shirt with a train token tied to a zipper pull. In conversation Irene listens with the head tilted a little to the left.
personality: Irene is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. Irene loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
agenda: To replace the shirt without blaming the washers.
family: Mia Nair is Irene’s first cousin once removed. Irene offers the first invitation. Mia gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The clean ledger*, Mia says, “I want to be the last name he reads. I owe him an apology he never put in his ledger.”
connections: Russell Hooper. A useful lullaby depends on choosing the right machine and the right load.
